title: Shortest Clear Path in a Binary Matrix
statement: You are given an n x n grid where each cell is 0 (open) or 1 (blocked). A clear path starts at the top-left cell (0, 0), ends at the bottom-right cell (n-1, n-1), and steps only through open cells. From a cell you may move to any of its up to eight neighbors (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) as long as that neighbor is open. The length of a path is the number of cells it visits, counting both the start and end cells. Return the length of the shortest clear path. If no such path exists, return -1; this includes the case where the start cell or the end cell is itself blocked. For a single-cell grid [[0]] the answer is 1.
hints: The grid is an implicit graph: each open cell links to its open neighbors. Which traversal finds the fewest steps in an unweighted graph?

Run BFS from (0, 0). The neighbor set has eight offsets (including all four diagonals), and you must mark a cell visited the moment you enqueue it, not when you pop it, so it never enters the queue twice.

Guard the blocked-endpoint cases first (return -1 if grid[0][0] or grid[n-1][n-1] is 1). Seed the queue with (0, 0, 1), and for each dequeued cell try all eight offsets; the first time you dequeue (n-1, n-1) its stored distance is the answer. If the queue drains without reaching it, return -1.
